findings.source_quote: Ἄκουσον, [φησίν,] ἐν ποίοις ἔργοις θανατοῖ ἡ ἐπιθυμία ἡ πονηρὰ τοὺς δούλους τοῦ Θεοῦ.
findings.english_quote: Bounded Athos and Latin alternatives are separately disclosed in reader notes.
findings.issue: The metadata claims disclosure that the supplied reader notes do not contain. No bounded Athos or Latin alternative wording is presented, so readers cannot identify or compare those purported alternatives.
findings.suggested_revision: Remove this claim unless the relevant alternative wording and its provenance are supplied. Describe only the bracketed attribution and lexical alternatives actually disclosed; retain the selected working reading.

findings.english_quote: The working i.3 brackets he says; the 1891 apparatus calls it Harmer’s insertion supported by versions, while Lake (1907) Plate VIII lacks it. The English supplies the disclosed working attribution, not a claim of unanimous Greek.
findings.issue: The supplied source establishes the brackets, but does not establish the assertions about Harmer, versional support, or Lake’s plate. The note presents those historical and visual-source claims categorically without supplied supporting evidence. The attribution itself is appropriately disclosed as supplied and need not be removed.
findings.suggested_revision: Retain the directly supported disclosure: “The selected working Greek brackets ‘he says’; the English includes this bracketed attribution.” Supply an attributable apparatus excerpt and supporting transcription or image evidence for the additional claims, or explicitly identify them as unverified reports rather than established collation results.

findings.source_quote: μάλιστα δὲ ἐὰν ἐμπέσῃ εἰς αὐτὴν δοῦλος Θεοῦ καὶ μὴ ᾖ συνετός, δαπανᾶται ὑπ’ αὐτῆς δεινῶς.
findings.english_quote: If a servant of God[c] falls into it and is not sensible, it consumes him terribly.
findings.issue: The conditional and negation are preserved, but μάλιστα, “especially,” is omitted. This removes the source’s explicit emphasis linking this particular case to the preceding general assertion about consumption.
findings.suggested_revision: For fresh review: “This is especially so if a servant of God[c] falls into it and is not sensible: it consumes him terribly.”

findings.source_quote: Ἄκουσον, [φησίν,] ἐν ποίοις ἔργοις θανατοῖ ἡ ἐπιθυμία ἡ πονηρὰ τοὺς δούλους τοῦ Θεοῦ.
findings.english_quote: Bounded Athos and Latin alternatives are separately disclosed in reader notes.
findings.issue: Independently of the standard edition, this edition also claims reader-facing disclosure of Athos and Latin alternatives that its supplied notes do not actually present.
findings.suggested_revision: Remove the claim or supply the specific alternatives with their provenance. Do not substitute an undisclosed variant for the selected working text.

findings.english_quote: The working i.3 brackets he says; the 1891 apparatus calls it Harmer’s insertion supported by versions, while Lake (1907) Plate VIII lacks it. The English supplies the disclosed working attribution, not a claim of unanimous Greek.
findings.issue: The brackets and editorial status are disclosed correctly, but the categorical apparatus and plate claims cannot be established from the supplied working transcription. Reusing the standard note does not independently substantiate them.
findings.suggested_revision: Keep the bracketed-attribution disclosure. Provide supporting apparatus and witness evidence for the historical claims, or qualify them as unverified reports. No change to the included speaker attribution is required merely because an alternative is reported.

summary: The standard main text covers the selected Greek faithfully, including its conditions, negations, death assertions, and disclosed bracketed attribution. The simplified text additionally loses the explicit “especially” emphasis. Both editions require correction of unsupported or absent alternative-disclosure claims. Reader-facing “servant” follows current policy. This review assesses the supplied working transcription and English materials, not unseen editions, manuscript handwriting, or exhaustive collation; proposed wording still requires fresh review.
